names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Συμεών ηγούμενος Ιεράς μονής Φιλοθέου Αγίου Όρους ο Μονοχίτων και Ανυπόδητος», with the rank word, the office and the two epithets left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's fifth heading for the Julian 19 April, „Преп. Симеон Боси.“, with Преп. left off, which is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`. **Боси is kept**: it is not in `BRIEF-SERBIAN.md` §5's table of rank words but the by-name the entry explains in so many words — he went barefoot and for that he was called Боси — and it is what this folder's English name carries as «the Barefoot». Keeping it also holds the form out of a fold: `simeon-of-persia` has held a bare Serbian «Симеон» since the Julian 17 April of this wave.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Απριλίου — «Όσιος Συμεών ηγούμενος Ιεράς μονής Φιλοθέου Αγίου Όρους ο Μονοχίτων και Ανυπόδητος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page names his village Vathyrema of Agia, his father the priest Andreas and his mother Aikaterini, the monasteries Oikonomeion or Komnineion of Kissavos, the Great Lavra and Philotheou on Athos, and the Holy Trinity and Transfiguration of Flamouri on Pelion which he built. Its chronology does not hold together: it makes him die in 1594 aged over a hundred, has him heal the daughter of sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, who died in 1566, and dates the building of Flamouri to the patriarchate of Kallinikos III of Zagora — and it reconciles none of this, so only the death year it states was taken. Under «Ιερά Λείψανα» it puts his skull at the monastery of Flamouri in Magnesia and portions at Komnineion of Larissa and at St Gerasimos of Zagora. The apolytikion it prints is the common of a venerable father, under his name and naming him.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 02.05.2026 (19. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Симеон Боси.“

attestations.note: The day's fifth entry, on the same menologion day the Greek keeps him on. **No date was added and none changed**: the entry says only that he reposed in Constantinople and prints no year at all, where this folder already holds saint.gr's 1594 and its «in the City». New from the entry: that he **strengthened the Christians in the faith in many Balkan lands** and **was glorified by wonderworking**, and the reason for the by-name in the Prologue's own words — **he went barefoot, and for that he was called the Barefoot**. That he was for a short time abbot of Philotheou agrees with the `office` this folder already carries. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Ταῖς τῶν δακρύων σου ροαῖς, τῆς ἐρήμου τό ἄγονον ἐγεώργησας καί τοῖς ἐκ βάθους στεναγμοῖς, εἰς ἐκατόν τούς πόνους ἐκαρποφόρησας καί γέγονας φωστήρ, τῆ οἰκουμένη λάμπων τοῖς θαύμασι, Συμεών Πατήρ ἡμῶν Ὅσιε, πρεύσβευε Χριστῶ τῶ Θεῶ, σωθῆναι τᾶς ψυχᾶς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, on the page of «Όσιος Συμεών ηγούμενος Ιεράς μονής Φιλοθέου Αγίου Όρους ο Μονοχίτων και Ανυπόδητος». It is the common of a venerable father, printed under his name and naming him.

english.text: With the streams of thy tears thou didst make the barren desert fruitful, and with thy sighs from the depths thou didst bring thy labours to fruit a hundredfold, and thou becamest a luminary, shining upon the world with wonders, O Symeon our venerable father. Intercede with Christ God that our souls be saved.
